issues.legal_issue: A final eviction permission obtained under the former rent-control regime requires eviction under the transitional regime without a fresh inquiry into the original ground, notwithstanding the tenant’s death during the proceedings.
material_facts: The landlord obtained permission to seek eviction on the ground of personal need, and that permission was ultimately upheld and became final.
After the new regime took effect, the landlord sought an eviction order under its transitional procedure.
The tenant died while proceedings were pending; the landlord applied to bring the tenant’s heirs on record, and later filed a further eviction application.
The court found no failure by the landlord to take steps concerning substitution.
issues.conclusion: The eviction order was proper. Once the required permission had become final, the prescribed authority had to order eviction and could not reconsider whether the original ground existed afresh; the tenant’s death did not invalidate the order in these circumstances.
issues.legal_principle: Section 43(2)(rr) of the U.P. Urban Buildings (Regulation of Letting, Rent and Eviction) Act, 1972 requires the prescribed authority to order eviction where permission under section 3 of the former Act was obtained on a ground specified in section 21 and became final; it expressly dispenses with a fresh inquiry into that ground. The court approved Bansilal Sahu v. The Prescribed Authority and distinguished the possibility of reopening a concluded matter by relying on the finality principle in Syed Asadullah Kazmi v. The Additional District Judge.

rule.if: transitional_eviction_proceeding and prior_permission_final and permission_ground_covered and landlord_pursued_eviction_after_tenant_death and transitional_rule_requires_eviction

predicates.transitional_eviction_proceeding: The landlord pursued eviction through a procedure for carrying forward a permission obtained under an earlier rent-control regime.
predicates.prior_permission_final: The permission to seek eviction had become final under the applicable proceedings.
predicates.permission_ground_covered: The final permission rested on a ground that the current eviction procedure recognizes.
predicates.landlord_pursued_eviction_after_tenant_d: The tenant died during the proceedings, and the landlord continued pursuing eviction, including by seeking to bring heirs on record and filing a further application.
predicates.transitional_rule_requires_eviction: The governing transitional scheme requires an eviction order once the qualifying permission has become final, without a fresh determination of the original ground.

issues.definition: When a transitional eviction proceeding rests on final qualifying permission and the governing scheme requires eviction without a fresh ground inquiry, the authority must order eviction even if the tenant dies during the proceedings and the landlord continues pursuing the claim.

issues.legal_issue: Later events do not defeat a final eviction order when the governing transitional scheme bars reconsideration of the established need and the events do not materially alter that need.
material_facts: The landlord had obtained a final eviction order based on a need to occupy the premises after retirement.

An agreement to sell part of the property to a family member of the tenant stated that the landlord’s need continued; the sale was not completed, and the purchaser did not proceed to execute the sale deed.
The court considered the effects of restrictions on transfer and increased building costs, and found that the landlord’s need had not been met or shown to be capable of being met otherwise.
The alleged agreements to sell the premises to other purchasers were not proved to have been acted upon or given effect.
The court found that the later events had not materially altered the position so as to defeat the final order.
issues.conclusion: The subsequent events did not defeat the landlord’s need or justify disturbing the final eviction order, and the appeal was dismissed.
issues.legal_principle: Courts may ordinarily take cautious account of later events to mould relief, subject to fairness to both sides: Pasupuleti Venkateswarlu v. The Motor & General Traders and Hasmat Rai v. Raghunath Prasad. But a concluded eviction matter cannot be reopened where finality has attached, and section 43(2)(rr) specifically bars a fresh inquiry into the ground once the qualifying permission has become final. The court relied on Syed Asadullah Kazmi and approved the approach in Bansilal Sahu; it also noted that, on the facts, the later events did not materially alter the landlord’s need.

rule.if: transitional_eviction_proceeding and eviction_order_final and later_sale_agreements_uncompleted and landlord_need_persisted and alternative_sale_unproved and transitional_rule_bars_fresh_need_review

predicates.transitional_eviction_proceeding: The landlord pursued eviction through a procedure for carrying forward a permission obtained under an earlier rent-control regime.
predicates.eviction_order_final: The order for eviction had become final in the relevant proceedings.
predicates.later_sale_agreements_uncompleted: Agreements made after the original eviction proceedings did not result in a completed sale of the premises relied on to defeat eviction.
predicates.landlord_need_persisted: The landlord’s stated need to occupy the premises continued and had not been met by the later events.
predicates.alternative_sale_unproved: Alleged alternative sales were not shown to have been acted upon or completed.
predicates.transitional_rule_bars_fresh_need_review: The governing transitional scheme bars a fresh inquiry into the eviction ground after the qualifying permission has become final.

issues.definition: When a final eviction order concerns a transitional proceeding, the landlord’s need persists, later sale arrangements are uncompleted or unproved, and the governing scheme bars a fresh review of need, those later events do not defeat the order.
